name: Pap and Chakalaka
summary: Firm maize porridge served with chakalaka, a warm relish of peppers, carrot, beans and curry spice.
story: Pap is the maize porridge at the centre of everyday South African meals, and it appears at nearly every braai (barbecue). Chakalaka is a spicy vegetable relish said to have grown from the townships around Johannesburg. Together they accompany grilled meat such as boerewors, or are eaten on their own.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the peppers and carrots and cook 6 minutes, stirring, until they begin to soften. They should keep a little bite.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Stir in the curry powder and chilli and cook 1 minute until the spices smell toasty, adding a splash of water if they stick.

steps.title: Simmer the relish
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, beans, salt and sugar. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, uncovered, until thick, glossy and the carrots are tender. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: While the relish simmers, bring 3 cups of the water and the salt to a boil in a heavy pot. Mix the remaining 1 cup of cold water with 1/2 cup of the maize meal to make a slurry.

steps.title: Make the porridge
steps.text: Stir the slurry into the boiling water and cook 5 minutes until it thickens and looks like loose porridge. Slowly rain in the remaining maize meal, stirring, until you have a thick mound.

steps.title: Steam to stiff pap
steps.text: Reduce the heat to very low, cover, and cook for 20 to 25 minutes without stirring. The pap is done when it has a stiff texture and no raw maize taste; fold in the butter if using.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Dish the pap in mounds or press into a wet bowl and turn out. Serve with a generous spoonful of warm chakalaka alongside.

tips: Make the slurry first to avoid lumps; lumpy pap is the most common mistake.
Keep the pap at a very low heat once covered, or it sticks and burns on the base.
Chakalaka keeps for a week in the fridge and is good cold on sandwiches.
For softer, creamy pap (slap pap), use 5 cups water instead of 4.

swaps.swap: Polenta or fine cornmeal is the closest alternative; it is yellow and slightly sweeter.
Use tinned haricot or kidney beans with an extra spoon of tomato paste.
A mix of cumin, coriander, turmeric and paprika works if you have no curry powder.
